notes: Iceland (IS) is not on the Global Constraints single-unit-exception list, yet is modeled here as one region. Reasoning: ~64% of the population lives in the Reykjavík capital area, and no second city (Akureyri, ~19,000) approaches a comparable diversified industrial base or cultural-hub status; Iceland is also linguistically and culturally homogeneous with no internal regionalist movement. It is therefore treated as a de-facto single unit while explicitly NOT added to the formal exception list, per the zone brief's instruction to state the reasoning rather than silently reclassify it.

Norrland (northern Sweden) was assessed against the three-part inclusion test and included as its own region despite lacking one dominant metropolis (Umeå, Sundsvall and Luleå are comparably sized secondary poles). It passes on the strength of a genuine regionalist identity ('Norrlandsfrågan'), a highly diversified industrial base (hydropower, forestry, mining), and its sheer land area (~half of Sweden). This is flagged as a softer pass than the zone's other, single-metro-anchored regions.

Mainland Småland (Jönköping, Kronoberg, Kalmar counties) has no dedicated mandate in the zone brief and was folded into the Gothenburg/West Sweden region rather than left as a coverage gap, since NUTS2024 groups it at NUTS-2 (SE21) with Gotland — which must be split out per the Gotland-as-separate-island mandate — leaving mainland Småland without a natural standalone NUTS grouping distinct from West Sweden's economic orbit.

Two areas were deliberately left OUT of the zone-4 region set as coverage gaps rather than force-fitted into a neighboring identity: (1) Finland's eastern lakeland provinces (Etelä-Savo/Pohjois-Savo/Pohjois-Karjala, i.e. the Kuopio/Joensuu/Mikkeli 'Savo-Karelia' area) — genuinely distinct in dialect and identity from both the Oulu and Helsinki nodes, but not separately mandated, so excluded pending a dedicated inclusion-test pass in a future revision; (2) Svalbard and Jan Mayen (NO0B) — near-uninhabited Norwegian Arctic territories that fail the inclusion test outright (no functioning urban cultural hub, no diversified industrial base beyond research/tourism outposts).

The Sápmi Indigenous homeland spans northern Finland, Sweden and Norway and is not congruent with any national or NUTS boundary. Rather than redraw national region boundaries, it is represented as a conflict_flag overlay on the Finnish Lapland/Sápmi region (fi-lapland-sapmi), with zone_nuts_codes spanning FI1D7 (Lappi), SE331/SE332 (Västerbotten/Norrbotten) and NO071/NO072/NO073 (Nordland/Troms/Finnmark) — deliberately overlapping the base nuts_codes of the Norrland and Tromsø/North regions, since conflict flags are overlays, not exclusive territorial claims.

Count tension: applying every fixed zone-4 mandate at face value (5 distinct Finnish nodes + Åland; 3 distinct Swedish nodes + Gotland + assessed Norrland; 2 Danish nodes; 5 distinct Norwegian fjord-culture nodes; Iceland; 3 Baltic single units; Greenland + Faroe Islands) yields 24 regions, above the zone brief's 'roughly 18-22' estimate. Per the Global Constraints instruction to flag rather than silently truncate such tension, this is noted explicitly here instead of merging any of the individually mandated, identity-distinct nodes to hit the lower estimate.

Norway's SR2024 county geometry reflects the 2024 restructuring following the 2020-2024 Viken/Troms-og-Finnmark mergers being reversed back into Østfold, Akershus, Buskerud, Troms and Finnmark as separate counties; the no-oslo-eastern-southern-norway region's population figure sums these post-2024 county boundaries rather than the short-lived 2020-2023 merged-county structure.

Svalbard and Jan Mayen (Norwegian Arctic territories, NUTS code NO0B) are deliberately excluded from this zone's region set: near-uninhabited, no functioning urban cultural hub, no diversified industrial base beyond research/tourism outposts, and outside this dataset's practical-regions scope (methodology note, not a silent coverage gap).

NUTS-vintage policy: authored nuts_codes in this file follow the GISCO 2024 geometry vintage (NUTS_RG_20M_2024_4326.geojson) wherever the NUTS 2027 recoding (reflected in the xlsx used for data/nuts_index.json) has since renumbered a country's units -- e.g. Norway's 2024 county-geometry codes (NO02/06/07/08/09/0A1/0A2/0A3) rather than the 2027-sheet's NO0C/D/E; the same policy applies to Belgium's 2024-vintage BE21/23 (vs. the 2027 recoding's BE26/27) and Bulgaria's BG3/BG4-vs-BG5x recoding elsewhere in this dataset. This keeps every authored code resolvable against the committed geometry file rather than a future labeling vintage the pipeline cannot yet render.

draft_v0.1.2 schema v2 migration: variant_group/variant_role removed; default_visible added (all zone4 units remain default_visible true -- no variant sets are mandated for the Nordics/Baltics in this content wave, so data/variant_sets/zone4.json is an empty array). pole (with mandated central_coord/secondary_coord per Amendment A1.4), parliament, and lang_family added to every unit. autarky.rationales added for water/food/energy on every unit per Amendment A1.6 (other four dimensions left for a future beta pass).

A1.10 Norrland split (draft_v0.1.2, new): se-norrland is split at the Sami-homeland (Sapmi) line, mirroring the Finnish/Norwegian pattern of giving the Sapmi-zone north its own unit. se-norrland-upper (SE33: Vaesterbotten+Norrbotten, Umeaa/Lulea) sits within the same Sapmi conflict_flag overlay already shared with fi-lapland-sapmi and no-tromso-north-norway. se-norrland-lower (SE31+SE32: Vaernland/Dalarna/Gaevleborg + Vaesternorrland/Jaemtland, Sundsvall/Oestersund) absorbs SE31 ('Norra Mellansverige') for coverage continuity, since the plan's own wording named only SE32 explicitly ('Sundsvall/Oestersund') -- SE31 is not separately mandated a home and would otherwise become a silent coverage gap; flagged here as an editorial inclusion rather than a literal mandate.

Innlandet / no-alesund-northwest reallocation -- UNSATISFIABLE AT LITERAL GRANULARITY (draft_v0.1.2 content-wave finding, flagged not silently resolved): the plan asks for a 'reasoned reallocation' giving Aalesund/Northwest Norway 'more of Innlandet' via 'adjust NUTS-3 code assignment'. Verified against the committed 2024 GISCO geometry (pipeline/raw/NUTS_RG_20M_2024_4326.geojson): Innlandet ships as a single undivided NUTS-3-equivalent feature (NO020) under NO02, with no finer sub-code available to split between the historically west-facing Gudbrandsdalen/Rauma-corridor communities (Dombaas-Aandalsnes, genuinely oriented toward Aalesund via the Rauma railway/E136) and the east-facing Hedmark/central-Gudbrandsdalen communities (oriented toward Oslo via the Mjosa/E6 corridor). Moving the entire NO02 code to no-alesund-northwest would misassign Hedmark, which is clearly Oslo-facing; moving nothing would ignore the mandate outright. Resolution taken: the NUTS code stays with no-oslo-eastern-southern-norway (unchanged), and no-alesund-northwest instead carries a documented `reach` entry into the Gudbrandsdalen/Rauma corridor (functional/cultural reach, not a territorial code reassignment). This item could not be honored literally without either a finer geometry source or an honest all-or-nothing code move that would misrepresent Hedmark; flagged for the controller/audit per the project's standing convention of stating such tensions rather than silently truncating or forcing an incorrect reallocation.

regions.name: Helsinki-Uusimaa
regions.identity_basis: Finland's capital region and its southeastern hinterland (Kanta-Häme, Päijät-Häme, Kymenlaakso, Etelä-Karjala); bilingual Finnish/Swedish administrative and cultural core distinct from the western and eastern-Finnish dialect areas.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, sum of Helsinki-Uusimaa (FI1B1) plus Kanta-Häme, Etelä-Karjala, Päijät-Häme and Kymenlaakso (FI1C2/5/6/7)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Helsinki metro >1.5M; national government, Nokia/ICT cluster, University of Helsinki
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: software and telecoms, finance/insurance, container/energy port at Kotka-Hamina, cross-border trade with Russia (historically) via Lappeenranta/Imatra
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong capital-region identity and southeastern border-province identity within Finland; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 FI1 (Manner-Suomi) treats all mainland Finland as one unit; split here into five Finnish nodes (Helsinki, Turku, Tampere/Western Finland, Oulu, Lapland/Sápmi) per the zone mandate, with Kanta-Häme/Päijät-Häme/Kymenlaakso/Etelä-Karjala (NUTS-2 FI1C minus Varsinais-Suomi) grouped into the Helsinki commuter/functional region rather than left as an unassigned residual.

autarky.rationale: Dense transport/health infrastructure and strong service economy; food and energy depend heavily on the rest of Finland and imports, offset partly by Kymenlaakso's agriculture and Kotka-Hamina's energy-import terminal.

rationales.water: Lake- and groundwater-fed supply from the southern Finnish moraine belt is ample.
rationales.food: Kymenlaakso agriculture is real but the capital-region population outstrips it; net food-import-dependent overall.
rationales.energy: Grid- and gas-import-dependent as a dense capital region; Kotka-Hamina's energy-import terminal underlines this rather than offsetting it.

sources: Helsinki-Uusimaa Regional Council (Uudenmaan liitto) statistical yearbook

pole.note: Helsinki overwhelmingly dominates its southeastern hinterland.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; no regional parliament below the national Eduskunta. This region has an elected regional council (maakuntavaltuusto) with limited planning/healthcare powers, not a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Turku / Southwest Finland
regions.identity_basis: Finland's oldest urban settlement area and former capital; distinct Southwest-Finnish coastal identity with historic Swedish-speaking minority presence in the archipelago.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, Varsinais-Suomi (FI1C1)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Turku metro ~330,000; former national capital, Turku Castle/Cathedral, university city
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: cruise-ship building at Meyer Turku, biotech/pharma cluster, some of Finland's best arable farmland, Baltic ferry logistics
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Southwest-Finnish/archipelago identity and bilingual heritage within Finland; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 FI1C (Etelä-Suomi) groups Varsinais-Suomi with Kanta-Häme/Päijät-Häme/Kymenlaakso/Etelä-Karjala; split here so Turku stands as its own mandated node, with the remaining FI1C provinces folded into the Helsinki functional region.

autarky.rationale: Best agricultural land in Finland gives strong food self-sufficiency; shipbuilding and ferry logistics support transport, but energy is grid-imported and clothing manufacture is negligible.

rationales.water: Aura river and southwestern-archipelago groundwater are ample.
rationales.food: Some of Finland's best arable farmland; a genuine regional surplus.
rationales.energy: Grid-imported; no major domestic generation asset within the region.

sources: Regional Council of Southwest Finland (Varsinais-Suomen liitto)

pole.note: Turku is the clear urban hub of Varsinais-Suomi.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; regional council (maakuntavaltuusto) only, not a parliament.

regions.name: Tampere & Western Finland
regions.identity_basis: Finland's second-largest urban region and its western-coast hinterland, including Swedish-speaking Ostrobothnia; historic industrial ('Manchester of the North') identity distinct from Helsinki and Turku.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, sum of NUTS-2 FI19 (Länsi-Suomi: Pirkanmaa, Satakunta, Keski-Suomi, Etelä-Pohjanmaa, Pohjanmaa)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Tampere metro ~400,000; historic industrial city, now ICT/games and university hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: engineering/machinery, energy (Olkiluoto NPP in Satakunta), agriculture and food processing in Ostrobothnia, forestry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong regional pride ('Tampere spirit') and distinct Swedish-speaking Ostrobothnian coastal identity within Finland; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Olkiluoto nuclear plant (Satakunta) and Ostrobothnian farmland give this region unusually strong energy and food self-sufficiency for Finland; clothing manufacture remains negligible.

rationales.water: Kokemaenjoki/Tammerkoski river network is ample.
rationales.food: Ostrobothnian farmland gives above-average food production for Finland.
rationales.energy: Olkiluoto nuclear plant (Satakunta) gives this region an unusually strong domestic generation asset for Finland.

pole.note: Tampere is the largest city, but Vaasa/Seinaejoki (Ostrobothnia) remain genuine secondary poles.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; regional council only, not a parliament.

regions.name: Oulu & North Ostrobothnia
regions.identity_basis: Northern Finland's largest city and its immediate hinterland (Kainuu, Central Ostrobothnia); tech-industry identity distinct from both southern Finland and Sámi Lapland to its north.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, sum of Pohjois-Pohjanmaa (FI1D9), Kainuu (FI1D8) and Keski-Pohjanmaa (FI1D5)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Oulu metro ~250,000; Finland's fastest-growing city, University of Oulu, major tech hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: health/mobile tech spun out of the Nokia era, mining and bioeconomy in Kainuu, agriculture in Central Ostrobothnia
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct northern Finnish identity, proud of tech-hub status, within Finland; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 FI1D (Pohjois- ja Itä-Suomi) also includes Lappi (split here as its own mandated Lapland/Sápmi node) and the eastern lakeland provinces (Etelä-Savo, Pohjois-Savo, Pohjois-Karjala), which are left as an unassigned coverage gap pending their own inclusion-test pass (see zone notes).

autarky.rationale: Solid hydro/grid access and forestry-based energy; food and transport are moderate given the region's size and dispersed population relative to southern Finland.

rationales.water: Oulujoki river/hydropower network and boreal groundwater are ample.
rationales.food: Central Ostrobothnian agriculture is modest relative to the region's size.
rationales.energy: Solid hydro/grid access and forestry-based biomass keep this mid-tier.

pole.note: Oulu is Northern Finland's dominant city and tech hub.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; regional council only, not a parliament.

regions.name: Lapland / Sápmi
regions.identity_basis: Finland's Arctic north; home to the Finnish Sámi homeland (Sápmi), an Indigenous cross-border cultural area also spanning northern Sweden and Norway, distinct from both mainstream Finnish identity and southern administration.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, Lappi (FI1D7)

conflict_flags.description: Sápmi, the Indigenous Sámi homeland, spans northern Finland, Sweden and Norway and is not congruent with any national or NUTS boundary. This overlay flags the cross-border cultural area without redrawing national region boundaries; it may overlap the nuts_codes of the Norrland, Tromsø/North and other neighboring regions.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Rovaniemi ~65,000; administrative capital of Finnish Lapland and seat of the Sámi Parliament of Finland
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Arctic tourism, reindeer husbandry, Kemijoki hydropower, mining, forestry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Sámi Indigenous identity plus a broader Lappish regional identity, both dependent on rather than seeking independence from Finland

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 FI1D groups Lappi with Kainuu/Pohjois-Pohjanmaa (folded into the Oulu node here) and the eastern lakeland provinces; split out as its own mandated node reflecting the distinct Sámi/Arctic identity.

autarky.rationale: Abundant glacial/snowmelt water and strong Kemijoki hydropower; harsh climate and vast distances limit food production and transportation, while healthcare access is thinner than in southern Finland.

rationales.water: Abundant glacial/snowmelt water and strong Kemijoki hydropower.
rationales.food: Harsh Arctic climate limits food production to reindeer husbandry and small-scale farming; structurally low.
rationales.energy: Kemijoki hydropower cascade gives strong energy self-sufficiency for a sparsely populated region.

sources: Sámediggi (Sámi Parliament of Finland) — Sápmi boundary description

pole.note: Rovaniemi is the administrative capital of Finnish Lapland and seat of the Sami Parliament of Finland.

parliament.name: Saamelaiskaerajaet (Sami Parliament of Finland)
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state with no regional parliament, but the Sami Parliament of Finland (seated in Inari/Rovaniemi) has real cultural-autonomy competence over Sami affairs within this region -- a genuine partial exception worth the audit's attention.

regions.name: Åland Islands
regions.identity_basis: Autonomous, monolingually Swedish-speaking archipelago province with its own parliament, flag and demilitarized status; explicitly mandated as a separate island unit distinct from Gotland.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland / Government of Åland (ÅSUB) 2023 estimate

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Mariehamn ~11,700; seat of the autonomous Åland Parliament (Lagting) and shipping-registry hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: maritime shipping/ferry operations, tourism, fishing and small-scale agriculture
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: autonomous, Swedish-speaking, demilitarized province with a strong distinct identity, constitutionally dependent on Finland (not seeking independence)

autarky.rationale: Ferry-based transport and a small grid make Åland import-dependent for energy (submarine cable from Sweden/Finland); fishing and small farms support modest food self-sufficiency.

rationales.water: Small archipelago catchments are adequate for the small population.
rationales.food: Fishing and small-scale farming support modest food self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: A small island grid is import-dependent via submarine cable from Sweden/Finland.

sources: Government of Åland — Self-Government Act summary

pole.note: Mariehamn is the sole town and seat of the autonomous Aland Parliament.

parliament.name: Alands lagting
parliament.note: Autonomous province with its own legislative parliament (Lagting) under the Self-Government Act.

regions.name: Finnish Lakeland (Savo-Karelia)
regions.identity_basis: Eastern Finnish lakeland provinces (Etelä-Savo, Pohjois-Savo, Pohjois-Karjala) sharing a Savo/Karelian dialect continuum and lake-district identity distinct from both southern (Helsinki-Uusimaa) and northern (Oulu) Finland; previously an unassigned coverage gap in this zone (see zone notes), now given its own inclusion-test pass.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, sum of Etelä-Savo (FI1DA), Pohjois-Savo (FI1DB) and Pohjois-Karjala (FI1DC)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Kuopio (~123,000) is the largest single city and regional cultural anchor, but the lakeland is genuinely polycentric: Jyväskylä (just outside this region, in neighbouring Länsi-Suomi) and Joensuu/Lappeenranta are comparably-sized secondary poles rather than clear satellites of Kuopio -- flagged as a weak single-hub fit, mirroring the Calabria precedent in zone 3 (retained standalone rather than silently merged, since no adjacent region is a culturally honest merge target for the Savo/Karelian dialect area).
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: forestry and bioeconomy (pulp/paper, wood products), agriculture, lake-district tourism, and a significant higher-education/research base (University of Eastern Finland, split across Kuopio and Joensuu campuses)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Savo and Karelian dialect/identity area within Finland; no separatism, but a genuine cultural self-conception distinct from both Helsinki and Oulu

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 FI1D (Pohjois- ja Itä-Suomi) groups this lakeland area with Lappland/Sápmi (FI1D7) and Oulu/Kainuu/Central Ostrobothnia (FI1D9/FI1D8/FI1D5); split here into its own region on dialect and lake-district identity grounds, consistent with the zone's finer-than-NUTS-1 approach elsewhere.

autarky.rationale: Extensive hydropower access and forestry-derived biomass give strong energy self-sufficiency; the lake district's abundant fresh water is a genuine surplus resource. Food is moderate (agriculture present but not surplus-scale). Transportation lags due to a lake-fragmented geography and dispersed population outside Kuopio.

rationales.water: The lake district's abundant fresh water is a genuine surplus resource.
rationales.food: Agriculture present but not surplus-scale; moderate.
rationales.energy: Extensive hydropower access and forestry-derived biomass give strong energy self-sufficiency.

sources: University of Eastern Finland regional profile

pole.note: Genuinely polycentric per the region's own inclusion-test note; Kuopio is the largest single anchor.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; regional council only, not a parliament.

regions.name: Stockholm-Mälardalen
regions.identity_basis: Sweden's capital region and its Lake Mälaren functional hinterland; the country's dominant political, financial and university-and-manufacturing-belt core.
regions.population_note: Statistics Sweden (SCB) 2023 estimate, NUTS-1 SE1 (Östra Sverige: Stockholm, Uppsala, Södermanland, Östergötland, Örebro, Västmanland counties)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Stockholm metro >2.4M; national capital, Nasdaq Nordic, Kista Science City, largest Nordic ICT cluster
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: finance and fintech (Klarna, Spotify origin), ICT, university research (Uppsala), heavy manufacturing (ABB Västerås, Saab Linköping)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: clear Stockholm-region identity within Sweden; strong commuter integration with Mälardalen towns, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Excellent transport (rail, Arlanda) and healthcare infrastructure; grid access to national hydro/nuclear supports energy, while food security depends on the wider Mälardalen agricultural plain rather than the capital itself.

rationales.water: Lake Malaren and its river network give abundant supply.
rationales.food: Food security depends on the wider Malardalen agricultural plain rather than the capital itself; moderate.
rationales.energy: Grid access to national hydro/nuclear supports energy, though the capital's demand keeps this mid-tier.

pole.note: Stockholm overwhelmingly dominates its Malardalen hinterland.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Sweden is a unitary state; the region has an elected regional council (regionfullmaktige, mainly healthcare/transit competence), not a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Gothenburg & West Sweden
regions.identity_basis: Sweden's second city and west-coast maritime/industrial region, extended here to include the inland Småland provinces (Jönköping, Kronoberg, Kalmar) that share West Sweden's functional-economic orbit and lack a separately mandated node.
regions.population_note: Statistics Sweden (SCB) 2023 estimate, sum of Västsverige (NUTS-2 SE23: Västra Götaland, Halland) plus Jönköping, Kronoberg and Kalmar counties (SE211/212/213)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Gothenburg metro >1M; Scandinavia's largest port, Volvo headquarters
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive manufacturing, maritime logistics, textile/design cluster (Borås), Småland furniture and glassworks industry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct West-Swedish maritime identity and separate Småland provincial identity ('Smålandsanda'), both dependent on Sweden; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 SE2 (Södra Sverige) groups Västsverige with Sydsverige (Skåne/Blekinge) and Småland-med-öarna (which includes Gotland); split here into Gothenburg/West Sweden (incl. mainland Småland), Malmö/Skåne and Gotland per the mandated distinct nodes, since NUTS2024 SE21 bundles mainland Småland with Gotland (SE214), which must stand alone.

autarky.rationale: Strong port/road logistics and a diversified industrial base (auto, textile, forestry) support most dimensions evenly; food security benefits from Småland's farmland and forestry economy.

rationales.water: Gota Alv and West Swedish lake network are ample.
rationales.food: Smaland's farmland and forestry economy give a solid regional food score.
rationales.energy: Grid- and hydro-supplied; diversified but not a major domestic generation surplus.

inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Medicon Valley life-sciences cluster (with Lund University), Sweden's most productive farmland, Karlskrona naval shipyards

regions.name: Lower Norrland
regions.identity_basis: Sweden's more temperate northern-to-central belt (Vaernland, Dalarna, Gaevleborg NUTS-2 SE31 + Vaesternorrland/Jaemtland NUTS-2 SE32), split out from the former se-norrland record per the draft_v0.1.2 Sapmi-line mandate: this half sits south of the Sami-homeland overlay zone and is culturally closer to Svealand, though it retains genuine Norrland regionalist sentiment ('Norrlandsfraagan').
regions.population_note: Statistics Sweden (SCB) 2023 estimate, sum of Norra Mellansverige (NUTS-2 SE31: Vaernland, Dalarna, Gaevleborg) and Mellersta Norrland (NUTS-2 SE32: Vaesternorrland, Jaemtland); the other half of the former se-norrland total (1,757,000).
regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 SE3 previously grouped this territory with SE33 as one se-norrland record; split in draft_v0.1.2 at the Sapmi line. SE31 (Vaernland/Dalarna/Gaevleborg, 'Norra Mellansverige') is included here rather than left as a coverage gap, since it borders SE32 directly and no other zone-4 record claims it; this keeps the two split halves summing exactly to the former se-norrland total.

pole.note: No single dominant metropolis; Sundsvall (coastal industrial hub) is the largest, with Oestersund/Karlstad/Falun as comparable secondary poles, mirroring the former se-norrland record's own polycentric-north honesty note.

inclusion_test.dependent_identity: genuine Norrland regionalist sentiment ('Norrlandsfraagan') within Sweden, distinct from but adjoining the Sami-homeland Upper Norrland to its north; no separatism

rationales.food: Vaernland/Gaevleborg farmland is more productive than the Arctic north, giving a moderate food score.
rationales.energy: Hydropower (Indalsaelven) and forestry biomass keep this region energy-strong.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1-equivalent NO0 treats all of Norway as one unit; split here into five nodes (Oslo & East/South, Stavanger-Bergen, Trondheim, Ålesund/Northwest, Tromsø/North) per the mandated fjord-culture distinctions. Eastern/southern Norway (NO08 Oslo og Viken, NO09 Agder og Sør-Østlandet, NO02 Innlandet) is grouped under Oslo as its dominant, commuter-linked metropolitan hinterland rather than given a separate un-mandated node. Note: the raw GISCO NUTS_RG_20M_2024 geometry file still ships pre-2024-restructuring NUTS2 groupings (NO02/NO06/NO07/NO08/NO09) rather than the newer SR2024 NO0C/NO0D/NO0E scheme listed in data/nuts_index.json; codes here were adjusted to match the actual geometry, per the build pipeline's resolution requirement.

reach.note: The Rauma railway line and E136 road connect Aalesund/Moere og Romsdal westward into northwestern Innlandet (the historic Romsdal-facing Gudbrandsdalen communities). This is documented here as a functional/cultural reach ONLY, not a territorial reassignment: per the draft_v0.1.2 plan's request to give this region 'more of Innlandet', the bulk of Innlandet (Hedmark and central Gudbrandsdalen, oriented toward Oslo via the Mjosa/E6 corridor) remains genuinely Oslo-facing, and the committed 2024 GISCO geometry ships all of Innlandet as a single undivided NUTS-3-equivalent code (NO020) with no finer sub-split available -- so a literal partial NUTS-3 code move is not possible without a different geometry source. Flagged as an unsatisfiable-at-current-granularity item rather than forcing an all-or-nothing code move that would misassign Hedmark.
